GA-105Code Editor · D2for Jefsev's review

The Editor

The design of research §5.2: the sidebar's Editor section, the folder picker, the Editor page with its tree, tabs, code and status bar, search in the folder, behind main and Update, a person's card, changed on disk, and Settings → Editor folders. F2 builds the page and the sidebar, F3 behind main, F4 a person's card.

Every screen is drawn with the app's own stylesheets (src/styles), so it looks as the app will; the new components are in editor.css, written for F2 to move into components.css, and the new tokens in editor-tokens.css. The code's colours use D1's token names (syn-*): D1 isn't approved yet, so their values here are placeholders. Each screen shows dark, then light; the switch shows one theme. Hover a control for its tooltip. Built by node design/code-editor/gen-editor.mjs.

1. The sidebar's Editor section

Between Projects and Agents, a section that folds like Agents and Memory (GA-90's FoldSection, with "editor" added to Fold and kept in localStorage with the others). Its rows are the folders you opened, newest first, at most 8.

  • Heading. “Editor”; + opens the folder picker (§2), the caret folds the section. Folded, the heading says how many folders are behind main, as folded Agents says how many agents are live.
  • A row. Lucide folder-code, the folder's name, and on the right one word on how it stands, in text-3: behind first (“3 behind”), else changed (“4 changed”), else ahead (“1 ahead”), else nothing. The full standing and the folder's path are in the row's tooltip. Words, not arrows: the arrows were a short form, and a word is as short here.
  • A card's worktree shows the card's identifier (mono) and title. Pinned to you: “by hand” with Lucide keyboard. An agent working on it now: the pulse (teal: an agent at work, its one meaning) and “read-only”. Lowercase, like Agents' “paused”.
  • Update running: a turning loader-circle and “updating”. Selected: the folder the Editor page shows, with the selected fill like every page's row. Hover: the hover fill.
  • Right click (or the context menu key) on a row: Open in VS Code, Zed or PhpStorm (only those found), Copy path, Remove from the list; a card's row adds Open card. No ⋯ button on the row: a button inside a row that is a link isn't allowed, and the row stays quiet.
  • Empty: one row, “Open a folder”, which opens the picker.

2. Opening a folder: the folder picker

+ on the Editor heading opens it, and so does Open a folder on the Editor page when no folder is open (#/editor, behind it here). A popover like the @ picker, 380px wide, beside the sidebar: its top at the heading, moved up as far as it must to fit the window (fixed, through a portal, since the sidebar clips what overflows it).

  • One box filters all groups as you type. ↑ and ↓ choose, Enter opens, Escape closes. A folder already in the sidebar opens there; a new one goes to the top of the list.
  • Projects: each active project's linked folder, with the project's colour dot, as in the sidebar. In ~/Herd: the folders directly inside it that aren't a project's; one group per folder in Settings → General → Editor folders. Cards: worktrees that exist, yours first: the column's glyph, the identifier, the title, and how it stands (“by hand”, or the pulse and who is working).
  • On the right, where the folder is (mono, text-3, cut off at the start of the line when long). A folder outside these places opens only through a project: the footer says where to add one.

3. The Editor page

#/editor/<folder>. The top bar is the folder's: its breadcrumbs, how it stands against main, Fetch and Open in. Under it, the file tree (260px; its button or Ctrl+B folds it) beside the tabs and the code. At the bottom, the status bar, which is the open file's. Under the top bar there is room for one bar about the folder (§5, §6, and read-only below); under the tabs, one about the open file (§7, and read-only below).

  • Top bar. Editor / gizai (the path in its tooltip), then the branch in mono and how it stands in words, separated by ·: “up to date with origin/main”, “3 behind origin/main”, “1 ahead”, “4 changed”. Fetch fetches now; its tooltip says when it last did. Open in lists the editors found on this computer; each opens the folder, at the open file and line.
  • Left panel. Files | Search on top (a segmented control: Search is §4), Go to file (Ctrl+P) as a box, then the folder's name with New file, New folder and Fold every folder, then the tree. Folders first, then files, each A to Z without regard to case; dotfiles show, .git never.
  • The tree (sizes and states in §9): ignored folders greyed and folded, their files read-only; an ignored file elsewhere, such as .env, greyed but it opens and saves as usual. git's mark on the right: a letter in its colour (M, A, R, U, C) with the word as tooltip; a folder that holds changes gets a dot. File icons by kind only (code, JSON, text, .env, image, other), all text-3: colour stays for meaning.
  • Tabs: the file's name (and its folder when two have the same name, like the two README.md), git's mark, × or a dot while not saved; middle click or Ctrl+W closes. The open tab joins the code under it, with an accent line on top. Tabs are kept per folder on this computer.
  • The code: CodeMirror in the app's mono font (Settings → Appearance), t-code (12.5/20, growing with the Interface size), line numbers in text-3, the active line on hover, matching brackets, fold carets that show when the gutter is hovered, no wrapping. Colours: D1's syn-* tokens (placeholders here).
  • Status bar: the file's path and git status on the left; the cursor (a button: go to line), line endings, language and whether it's saved on the right. Not saved is a button that saves.
  • Fonts. Names in the tree and on tabs are in the interface font, like the Memory page's tree; paths (status bar, picker, bars), branches and identifiers are mono, as machine values are everywhere in Gizai.
  • Edit anyway is the Editor's own question: the backend lets you write in a worktree no agent works on (readOnly false), and the Editor asks first when the card isn't yours. While an agent works on it, the backend refuses writes (readOnlyWhy), and the bar says who.

Go to file, find and replace, Open in

Go to file (Ctrl+P) is the command palette's look over the Editor: matching files, the match in bold, each file's folder after it. Find and replace (Ctrl+F) is @codemirror/search's panel on top of the code, drawn with the app's inputs: Match case, Words and Regular expression inside the box, “3 of 4”, previous and next, then Replace and Replace all. Open in lists only the editors found, each with the command it found.

The tree's menu, New file, Delete

Right click on a row (or the context menu key, or Shift+F10): New file, New folder, Rename (F2), Delete, Copy path, Open in. New file and Rename type in place; a path makes its folders (app/Exports/InvoicesCsv.php). Delete asks under the row, in one sentence, never with a dialog; Enter or the button deletes, Escape cancels.

Read-only: a card's worktree

A card's worktree is read-only while an agent works on it, and editable when the card is yours. On another's card with no agent at work, the Editor says whose it is and offers Edit anyway; your changes then wait, uncommitted, for the agent's next run. The bar takes the folder bar's place; the tabs show a lock, the status bar says why.

4. Search in the folder

Ctrl+Shift+F, or Search at the top of the left panel, puts the search in the tree's place; Files or Escape brings the tree back. It searches as you type (after 300 ms), with git grep over the files git tracks and new files it doesn't ignore.

  • The box with Match case, Words and Regular expression inside it, pressed like the Markdown toolbar's buttons. Under it, how many results; then the results by file: the file's name, its folder (text-3), how many hits; under it each hit's line number and line, the match marked as the Memory page marks its search hits.
  • A click (or Enter) opens the file at that line and marks the line for a moment; the result stays selected. A long line shows from a little before its match. At most 2,000 results and 10 seconds; then it says so.
  • Search in a file is Ctrl+F (§3); replacing across files waits for a later version.

5. Behind main, and Update

Gizai fetches main when the Editor opens a folder, every 10 minutes while it shows it, and on Fetch: the same fetch as a card's start, into the same ref. The top bar always says how the folder stands. When it is behind, a bar under the top bar says by how much, when it was fetched, and what Update will do, in the plan's own words. Update is a fast-forward of main and nothing else (checkout::plan, then checkout::update).

  • Update is the bar's one button, primary. Fetch is in the top bar only, so neither button is on screen twice; a failed fetch offers Try again in the bar.
  • Refused: the bar says why, in the plan's sentence after “Update can't run:”, and Update stays, turned off, with the same sentence as its tooltip. Nothing happens by surprise. The Editor never switches branches, so its refusal for another branch says to switch first, in a terminal or your own editor (the plan's own sentence is meant for the Team Lead).
  • Updating: the plan's words with a turning loader; Update and Fetch are off. Done: what it did, with a check in success, and Dismiss. Stopped: what failed and what it did before, on danger-soft, with the output to show.
  • The sidebar's row says “updating”, then loses its “3 behind” without a reload.
  • Contract C3 needs one more field for this: EditorUpdated.output (the end of the output when it stopped), for Show output. Everything else is in FolderMain and EditorUpdated as they are.

6. A person's card

A card assigned to you can be done by hand. Open in editor on the card makes its worktree as for an agent, pins the card to you so agents leave it alone, moves it to In progress, and opens the worktree here. A card bar then takes the folder bar's place: Commit…, Push and Hand over move it on as an agent's run would. On the board the card says “By hand” while it is pinned to a person.

  • On the card: Open in editor (Lucide square-code) in the top bar's actions, for a card assigned to you that no agent is working on; its tooltip says what it does. While the worktree is prepared (composer install, npm ci) it says so and turns. Off, with the reason, while an agent works on it. A card started by hand gets the “By hand” badge in its head; Open in editor then just opens it.
  • The card bar: the column's glyph, the identifier and title, the branch (mono, text-3), how far it is, then Commit…, Push and Hand over to Testing (to Review when the card's Testing switch is off). The button of the next step is primary: Commit… while there are changes, then Hand over, which pushes too. A button that can't act is off, with why as its tooltip.
  • Commit… opens a small box under it: the message, filled in with “KADE-41: Fix the invoice total”, and the files it commits (every change, as git sees it). Ctrl+Enter commits. What each button did shows in the bar in place of how far it is, for a few seconds.
  • Handed over: the bar says where it went; the worktree is read-only once QA works on it. Back from QA: the card is pinned to you again, and the bar says so in needs (magenta: a person is needed) until you open the card. F4 reads it from the card itself (back in In progress, its latest move by QA), with no new field.
  • On the board: the badge “By hand” (Lucide keyboard) before the person's avatar, never a working strip: no agent waits for it or works on it. The column's note doesn't count it.

7. Changed on disk

An agent, a terminal or another editor can change a file that is open here. The Editor asks every 3 seconds for the open files' versions. A tab you haven't touched reloads by itself, and the status bar says so for a few seconds. A tab with changes you haven't saved gets a bar over its code; Save refuses until you pick.

  • Reload shows the version on disk; your unsaved changes here are lost (its tooltip says so). Keep mine keeps your version; the next Ctrl+S then asks once more in the same bar, and the second one saves over the newer file.
  • Deleted on disk: Save it again writes your version back; Close tab drops it. With no changes here, the tab says the file isn't there any more (§3).
  • The bar uses the warning icon: a save could lose someone's work. Only the tab's file gets the bar, under the tabs; another tab with the same trouble gets its bar when it is opened.

8. Settings → General → Editor folders

Where your projects are. The folder picker lists every folder directly inside these (default ~/Herd); projects' linked folders and card worktrees open wherever they are. A section of General, after Updates and before Data, with the same rows as an agent's Folders: a path in mono, × to remove, Add folder, and Browse… for the system's folder picker.

  • Each row is checked as you type, with the refusals agent folders already have (folders.rs), written for this field. Under a good row: how many folders it holds and the first names, so you see what the picker will list. A missing folder is a warning, not a refusal: it may be a disk that isn't mounted.
  • Saved as soon as you add, change or remove one, like Settings' other lists. The Team Lead's copies (<data>/code) and Gizai's data folder never open, whatever is here.

On a narrow window

At the window's smallest, 900 px, 652 px stay beside the sidebar; at 1100 px, 852 px. The breadcrumbs keep their width and the standing gives way (cut off, the whole of it in its tooltip). A bar's sentence wraps beside its buttons, which go under it once less than 380 px is left for it; a person's card puts its branch under its title. The tree keeps its width and folds with Ctrl+B.

Dark

For screen readers and the keyboard

  • The tree is a tree of treeitems (aria-expanded on folders, aria-selected on the open file), with one tab stop: the arrows move, Enter opens, → and ← open and fold a folder.
  • The tabs are a tablist; each × is a button named “Close Sidebar.tsx”; a tab that isn't saved says so in its name (“Sidebar.tsx, not saved”).
  • A folder's bar is a status, a refusal or failure an alert; the status bar is a status, so “Saved” and “Reloaded” are read out.
  • Icons that carry meaning have words beside them or a name (the lock: “Read-only”); git's letters have their word as tooltip and name; nothing relies on colour alone.

10. Every text

A sentence that Gizai's backend makes (the plan's, git's) is shown as the Editor shows it. The status words on a sidebar row stay lowercase, like Agents' “paused” and “1 live”.
